payload.text: Oh, you're killing us. 5 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.
You again. Guantería Antigua. Thirty-three. Good card, better than you deserve.
Thirty-one. Last one, chaval. You say no, I pack up and we both go home. Chamberí stays with me.
Your numbers drift downward; mine do not follow. The Palacio de Cristal: one hundred fifteen. That is today's term, señor. Consider it at your leisure.

Ay, no, no, cariño, twenty? ¡Qué va! Five P, that is the price, and not one more. I don't rob children at my table, hijo. Here, take it. And listen — El Chato, next stall, opens for everybody at half past nine tonight. He likes honest traders like you.
Chamberí. Thirty-three. You want it, say so. I do not haggle with myself.
Thirty-three. I said it once. Card doesn't get cheaper because you say "fair."

Ay, hija, you insist on paying more! Está bien — six P, and that is my last word, eh? Not eighteen, por Dios. My Antonio would laugh at me. Take the card, and eat something later, you look thin. Six P, hecho.

"¡Catorce! Nando, this man throws pesetas like confetti!" — "Paco, we are honest brothers, we cannot take it." Five, hermano, cinco, and the Plaza del Dos de Mayo is yours. Last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella.

Say sí, the suitcase is closing.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 5 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh?
Look, 6 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
You move, I move. 33 P.
Two hundred forty is not a figure I asked for, señor. The Palacio de Cristal: one hundred nineteen. Each visit you lower; each visit I rise. Decide.
Two more. Impressive. Thirty-three. Still thirty-three. Card's selling fine without you.

Ay, cariño, fourteen! You will ruin yourself and make me rich, and that is not right. Six P, I said six, and six it stays. Take her home. And un consejo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates, hija.
One peseta. That is not moving, that is breathing. Chamberí stays thirty-three. Come back when you are serious.

"¡Amigo, amiga! Paco here—" "—and Nando, the handsome one. Look, look: Puesto del Rastro, a beauty, and for you only four P!" "Four! We practically give it away." "But quick, quick—the police... ehh, the *taxi* is waiting outside, motor running. Decide now or it drives off with the suitcase!"
Let's meet in the middle, cariño: 6 P.
You move, I move. 32 P.
Ciento veinticuatro for the Palacio de Cristal. That is my last word, señor. Refuse it, and I close the book and we are done.

"¡Twenty! Amigo, you have a generous heart—" "—too generous, we are honest men, Paco cries." "Four P, the price we said, no more. Take it!" "And quick—the team next door is waving money at us, but your face we like better." "The taxi's motor is running, hombre. ¡Vámonos!"
Two from you, one from me. Thirty-two. That's the math, amigo.
One peseta again. Fine. Thirty-one. I match what you give me, nada más. Chamberí is not getting cheaper by breathing at it.
¡Ay, diez! No, hija, no. Six P — that is my last word, de verdad. If you say no, I put her back in the box and we talk of other things, sin rencor. Six P, hecho. ¿Has comido algo hoy, cariño?

"¡Dieciocho! Nando, this man wants to ruin us with kindness—" "—we said four P, four P it stays, amigo. Our prices don't climb, they only run." "And run we must: one minute, the motor, the suitcase, ¡fuera! Say four and the Puesto del Rastro is yours, hombre. ¡Ya!"
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Chamberí. Thirty-three. You want it or you want to look?
Thirty-three. Same as before. You moved nothing, neither do I.

Ay, hola cariño, come, come — have you eaten yet? Sit a moment. Look, this one, Palacio de Velázquez, very pretty card, the glass palace in the Retiro. My favourite. For you, twenty-nine P. A good start for an album, hijo.

¡Amigo, amigo! Come, come — Paco, show him! Look: El Tatuador, fresh from the case, and for you, only 4 P.

And listen — this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on my brother's head. After this, nothing. Nando, tell him! Nothing left, nowhere. ¿Sí o no?

You again. Guantería Antigua, thirty-three. Good card, better than you think. Take it or walk.
¡Ja! ¿Veinte? Nando, ¿oíste eso? Amigo, we are pícaros, not thieves — four P, like I said, four. Paco, wrap it! Take it before my brother changes his mouth. El Tatuador, cuatro, hecho. ¿Sí?

Twenty-two. No. Thirty-three. I said it once already. Card does not get cheaper because you say "fair."

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten? Look here — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a beautiful card, one of my favourites. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with this very one, hijo.
One point from you, one from me. Thirty-two. That is how it works, amigo.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!

¡Amigo, basta! You keep climbing, we keep saying the same — cuatro P. Four! Paco already has it wrapped, the paper is on it, the string is tied. Don't insult us with sixteen, take El Tatuador for 4 P and we both go home smiling. ¿Hecho?

Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P. They stopped printing this one yesterday.
Two points. That is your big move? Thirty-three. Same as before. I do not chase.
Estación de Chamberí. Thirty-three. You've seen the stall, you know I don't haggle for fun.

Buenas, hijo! Have you eaten? Look, for you I have Samosas de la Plaza — twenty-nine primas, very pretty card. My late Paco always said it brought luck. And if you want better packs, El Chato next door opens for everybody at half past nine tonight.

Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres, pero no — five P, that is the price, and not one more. I would feel bad taking your money for a little card. Keep the rest for your album.

And listen, cariño: El Chato, next stall, opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. He likes honest traders like you.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
You move, I move. 33 P.
Buenas. You come at a quiet hour; good. El Ahuehuete is here, from my reserves. My terms: seven hundred sixty-one pesetas. I do not haggle quickly, señor.

¡Doce! Amigo, you keep paying us more and we keep saying no — ¿qué locura es esta? Bueno, last word, I swear: El Tatuador, cinco P. Cinco. Paco, the string, the paper, ya está. You say no, we close the case and walk. ¿Hecho o adiós?

Ay, cariño, twenty is a little thin. Come, let me say twenty-five primas for the Samosas de la Plaza and we are friends, eh? And listen — swap your duplicates with the other chicos; a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Eat something, hijo.
One peseta. That's not moving, that's twitching. Thirty-three.
Two from you, one from me. Thirty-two. That is how it works when you move slow.

¡Amigo, amiga! Paco here — and Nando, the handsome one. Come, come, look fast! Plaza del Dos de Mayo, four pesetas, straight from the case to your hands.

They stopped printing this one yesterday, hermano. Yesterday! No more coming, ever. We had three this morning... ¿Sí o sí?

Ay, cariño, qué cabezota eres — pero no. Cinco P, ni una más. Es una cartita, hijo, no un tesoro de museo. Guarda el resto para tus sobres.

Y vuelve mañana igual, que te cuento lo del abuelo y su álbum. ¿Has comido ya?
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more! A little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than the loose cards. Swap your duplicates!
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P. The team next door wants it, but we like you better.
Qué gusto, y sí, encontré la rana siendo niña — suerte no me faltó. Pero hablemos claro: por esas Samosas de la Plaza le ofrezco 16. Es lo que vale, ni un céntimo escondido.
Fifty-nine? No, señor. El Ahuehuete leaves this desk at seven hundred sixty-one pesetas. As for El Rastro al Amanecer — I keep my own counsel. Take your time deciding.

—¡Amigo, qué gusto! ¿Lazarillo de tu barrio? ¡Entonces eres de los nuestros!

—Mira, mira: Samosas de la Plaza, diez primas. Una ganga, ¿eh, Nando?

—¡Una ganga! Pero rápido, que nos vamos en un minuto, la maleta ya está cerrada y el tren no espera a nadie, hermano. ¿Sí o sí?
Two more from you. One from me. Thirty-one. You know the rhythm by now.

Ay, hija, qué testaruda eres, como mi nieta. Cinco P por la Plaza del Dos de Mayo, y es mi última palabra. Si no, guardo la cartita en la caja y hablamos de otra cosa, ¿eh?

Anda, ve a comer algo, cariño.

Dieciocho, veinte — amigo, you're throwing numbers like confetti! But listen, Nando's already closing the case. Four pesetas for the Plaza del Dos de Mayo. That's it, that's the last one, no more dancing.

Say sí now, or we walk to the next plaza and you never see it again.
One peseta again. You're pacing, not walking. Thirty-two. I already moved more than you did.
Chamberí. Thirty-three. You want it or you want to look?

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a moment — have you eaten? Look, this one, Plaza del Dos de Mayo, very pretty card. For you, 5 P.

And a little advice, hijo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates, always!

¡Eh, amigo, come, come! You have the face of a collector, Nando, no?

"The face of a winner, Paco!"

Look here — El Tatuador, the ink that never fades. Beautiful, sí? For you, only four P. Four! We leave at sunset, so... decide fast, campeón.
